data.content_ref: inline:The target's central cross-city claim — that the night-time gap scales with aridity (larger in more arid cities) — is contradicted by empirical UHI literature and by its own stated counterfactuals. Urban hydrology research consistently shows that irrigated, well-watered cities in arid regions (e.g., Phoenix, AZ) often exhibit LARGER nighttime UHI precisely because dry surroundings cool efficiently via radiative loss while dense urban irrigation and impervious thermal mass maintain warmer surface and air temperatures. The target even names this observation as a countercondition that would weaken its mechanism, so it cannot also assert that the gap unambiguously scales with aridity. By framing aridity as the single dominant modulator while acknowledging that arid irrigated cities may show maximal UHI, the target fails to identify the single mechanism that best explains cross-city variation, as the problem requires.
